title: Hypertension — WHO HEARTS/PEN baseline (draft)
summary: WHO/global baseline decision logic for hypertension diagnosis and primary-care management (HEARTS technical package / WHO 2021 HTN guideline). Universal logic every country inherits until a national overlay (drug choices to the national EML, target thresholds) is authored. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.

diagnosis.threshold: Office BP >=140/90 mmHg on two separate occasions.
diagnosis.highRiskThreshold: Consider pharmacotherapy at >=130/80 mmHg in established CVD, diabetes, or CKD.

management: Lifestyle for all: salt reduction, weight, physical activity, tobacco/alcohol cessation.
First-line classes: thiazide/thiazide-like diuretic, long-acting CCB (e.g. amlodipine), or ACE inhibitor / ARB.
Prefer a single-pill combination of two agents for most patients to reach target.
Avoid ACEi + ARB combination. ACEi/ARB are first choice in diabetes or CKD with albuminuria.
targets: High CVD risk / diabetes / CKD: <130/80 mmHg if tolerated.
redFlags: BP >=180/110 with symptoms (chest pain, breathlessness, neurological deficit, visual loss) — assess for hypertensive emergency and refer.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should map first-line agents to the national Essential Medicines List and adopt national target thresholds.

references.label: WHO Guideline for the pharmacological treatment of hypertension in adults, 2021
